rationale: A unanimous, doctrine-tight collateral-order decision is most likely assigned by the Chief to himself or to a consensus builder (Kagan/Barrett) to emphasize Cohen’s narrowness, separability, and effective-unreviewability limits, with Campbell-Ewald used to resist treating Yearsley as an immunity-from-suit. Separate writings are possible mainly to clarify that Yearsley remains available as a post-judgment defense and to caution against expanding interlocutory appeals in contractor litigation.
